compositionWarning: quarterly judgment counts range from 347 to 5523, a factor of 15.9. Every target below is a RATE, a SHARE or a RANK for that reason; no count is forecast, and a shift in what the publisher releases would still move a rate.

leadLag.note: LEAD-LAG ASSOCIATION, not influence. A provision both sides discover at the same time produces this pattern too.

doctrinalCompanionUniverse.note: the identity universe exists for 1444-1446 only and is bounded by authority.py's vocabulary, so this is an upper bound on how well a frozen companion set ages

newCodeUptake.note: commencement dates are not in the registry, so this is latency inside the published corpus, not latency from the day the code took effect.

decisionToPublicationLag.why: the corpus carries a decision date and our own retrieval timestamp. No publication date is held for any judgment, so the lag cannot be computed and is not approximated.

publicationProfile.warning: a shift in any of these near a deployment date is a publication-regime confound and must be reported BEFORE any doctrinal outcome, not alongside it.

speakerAwareRetrieval.note: coverage is recall over the court's own later citations. It is NOT a recommendation to retrieve whole judgments without role separation: the speaker programme measured what advocacy contributes to a whole-document count, and that contamination is exactly what partyOnlyPrecision prices.

companionsNotInFrozenSet.note: small because the identity universe has 28 members, not because doctrine is static

articleVersionSupersession.why: the corpus registry carries publication dates per INSTRUMENT, not per article version. Whether the text of article 16 at the time of a 1443 judgment differs from its text today cannot be answered from the metadata we hold, and this session does not reconstruct it.

instrumentTemporalValidity.why: only 2 of the registry's tracks carry a parseable hijri publication year, so the check would be computed over almost nothing. Reported as unsupported rather than as a zero.
instrumentTemporalValidity.limit: instrument level only. Article-version history is not held.

companionBackfill.purpose: fold count for companion persistence backtesting only. No historical claim is made across it and DOCTRINE.md still reads 1444-1446 alone.
